shots.line: Right now, outside the window of almost every airliner in the sky,
shots.scene: EST WIDE exterior: airliner cruising above a moonlit sea of clouds, window lights glowing, slow push

shots.line: the air is around minus fifty-five degrees Celsius.
shots.scene: Cabin window close: PAX in red hoodie at oval window, frost creeps across glass, -55°C readout pops on 'fifty-five'

shots.line: It's so thin that without oxygen, you'd have
shots.scene: Insert: oxygen mask drops from ceiling panel and swings, thin air dots drifting

shots.line: well under a minute of useful consciousness.
shots.scene: bigFace PAX scared, countdown ring 'UNDER 1 MIN' on 'minute'

shots.line: And yet, this is exactly where pilots want to be.
shots.scene: Cockpit wide from behind: PILOT (yellow cap) relaxed and smiling, sunrise glow through windscreen

shots.line: Thirty-five thousand feet.
shots.scene: TITLE CARD '35,000 FEET' over plane above clouds at dawn

shots.line: About ten and a half kilometers up.
shots.scene: Blueprint altitude column: plane marker rises to 10.5 KM

shots.line: Higher than Mount Everest, by more than a mile.
shots.scene: Everest silhouette, plane cruising well above it, dimension '+1 MILE'

shots.line: It's the number your captain announces on flight after flight.
shots.scene: Cabin wide: rows of seated passengers incl PAX, ceiling speaker pulses with rings (captain announcing)

shots.line: But why there?
shots.scene: bigFace PAX confused, glowing '?'

shots.line: Why not lower, where the air is warm and thick?
shots.scene: Low: warm thick hazy air, plane sinks into it, 'LOWER?' label

shots.line: Or higher, where it's even emptier?
shots.scene: High: near-black starry sky, plane rises, 'HIGHER?' label

shots.line: The answer is a balancing act.
shots.scene: Blueprint balance beam: plane on a see-saw, LOW vs HIGH weights tip and settle

shots.line: And once you see it, you'll never hear that announcement the same way again.
shots.scene: Medium: PAX in seat by window, golden light, leans back with knowing smile

shots.line: First: thin air is cheap air.
shots.scene: Chapter line 'THIN AIR = CHEAP AIR' over dusk sky

shots.line: Flying through air is a bit like wading through water.
shots.scene: PAX wading waist-deep through dusk sea, water pushes back, ripples

shots.line: Near the ground, it's thick, and it pushes back hard.
shots.scene: Blueprint: plane near ground in dense air dots, big DRAG arrows push back

shots.line: At thirty-five thousand feet, the air is only about a third as dense as at sea level.
shots.scene: Blueprint: two air boxes SEA LEVEL (dense) vs 35,000 FT (sparse), '≈ 1/3' on 'third'

shots.line: Less air pushing back means less drag.
shots.scene: Plane slicing through sparse air, drag arrow shrinks

shots.line: Less drag means less fuel.
shots.scene: Insert: cockpit fuel-flow gauge needle drops, 'LESS FUEL'

shots.line: And for an airline, fuel is one of the biggest bills there is.
shots.scene: Giant airline bill unrolls, FUEL line glows gold on 'bills'

shots.line: So why not just keep climbing forever?
shots.scene: Plane climbs steeply toward the stars, 'FOREVER?'

shots.line: Because the air that slows you down is also the air that holds you up.
shots.scene: Blueprint: plane with DRAG arrow back and LIFT arrow up, both labelled AIR

shots.line: Wings make lift by pushing air downward.
shots.scene: Blueprint airfoil: air streams bend downward, LIFT arrow rises on 'lift'

shots.line: Engines need air to burn their fuel.
shots.scene: Blueprint jet engine: AIR in + FUEL -> flame -> THRUST

shots.line: Thin it out too much, and the plane has to fly faster and faster just to stay in the sky.
shots.scene: 3D chase: low-poly airliner over cloud sea, speed readout climbing on 'faster'

shots.line: Climb high enough, and the slowest speed the plane can safely fly and
shots.scene: Medium: PILOT watches the speed tape, worried, instrument glow on face

shots.line: the fastest speed it's allowed to fly start squeezing together.
shots.scene: Blueprint speed band: MIN SPEED rises, MAX SPEED holds, gap squeezes

shots.line: Pilots have a grim name for that narrow gap.
shots.scene: bigFace PILOT grim, red warning glow

shots.line: The coffin corner.
shots.scene: 'COFFIN CORNER' slams in coral, narrow gap glows red

shots.line: So the plane hunts for a sweet spot.
shots.scene: Plane eases into a glowing 'SWEET SPOT' band above the clouds

shots.line: And up there, there's a bonus.
shots.scene: Cabin window: sun breaks above the clouds, PAX smiles

shots.line: Most of our weather lives in the lowest layer of the atmosphere, the troposphere.
shots.scene: Cross-section: storms, rain and clouds in the bottom layer, label TROPOSPHERE

shots.line: Its ceiling sits at roughly thirty-six thousand feet in the mid-latitudes.
shots.scene: Same cross-section: glowing ceiling line TROPOPAUSE, '~36,000 FT'

shots.line: Cruise near that ceiling, and you're above much of the rain, cloud, and chaos below.
shots.scene: Plane cruises in calm air above a storm deck, lightning flickers below

shots.line: Not all of it.
shots.scene: bigFace PILOT raises a brow: 'not all of it'

shots.line: The biggest thunderstorms punch even higher, which is why pilots still steer around them.
shots.scene: Giant thunderhead punches through the ceiling, plane banks around it

shots.line: Next, the wind.
shots.scene: Chapter line 'NEXT: THE WIND' with streaming wind lines

shots.line: Up here flow the jet streams, rivers of air that can race along at well over a hundred miles an hour.
shots.scene: 3D globe: glowing jet-stream ribbons circle the planet west to east, '100+ MPH'

shots.line: Ride one, and you arrive early on less fuel.
shots.scene: Plane rides a glowing wind ribbon, speed lines, 'EARLY' badge

shots.line: That's a big reason a flight from New York to London is often about an hour shorter than the trip back.
shots.scene: Blueprint map NEW YORK <-> LONDON: eastbound plane beats westbound, '≈ 1 HR SHORTER'

shots.line: And then, there's traffic.
shots.scene: Night sky full of blinking plane lights crossing in every direction

shots.line: In much of the world, eastbound flights cruise at odd thousands, like thirty-five thousand,
shots.scene: Blueprint lanes: FL350 -> EAST lights up

shots.line: and westbound flights at even ones, like thirty-six thousand.
shots.scene: Blueprint lanes: FL360 <- WEST added, planes pass

shots.line: Thousands of aircraft, stacked in invisible lanes.
shots.scene: 3D: stacked translucent lanes with dozens of planes sliding opposite ways, slow orbit

shots.line: But here's the twist. Thirty-five thousand isn't a magic number.
shots.scene: Twist: gold '35,000 FT' cracks and a red line slashes it on 'magic'

shots.line: It's a moving target.
shots.scene: Target reticle slides up and down the altitude axis

shots.line: A long-haul jet can take off carrying more than a hundred tons of fuel.
shots.scene: Runway at dusk: heavy airliner waits, fuel counter '100+ TONS'

shots.line: That makes it too heavy for its best altitude.
shots.scene: Blueprint: heavy plane with weight arrow, can't reach dotted BEST ALTITUDE

shots.line: So it starts lower. And as it burns fuel and gets lighter, it climbs, step by step.
shots.scene: Blueprint step-climb: plane climbs a staircase as fuel gauge drains

shots.line: Your plane literally rises higher as the flight goes on.
shots.scene: PAX watches seatback map: altitude number ticking up, awe

shots.line: So the next time your captain says, "We're cruising at thirty-five thousand feet,"
shots.scene: PILOT speaks into the mic: 'We're cruising at 35,000 feet', talk rings

shots.line: you'll know that number wasn't random.
shots.scene: bigFace PAX knowing smirk

shots.line: It was worked out for your plane's weight, today's winds, and the traffic around you.
shots.scene: Blueprint: WEIGHT, WINDS, TRAFFIC icons feed into 'FL350'

shots.line: A quiet calculation, made in freezing, thin air, more than a mile above the top of Everest.
shots.scene: Final wide: plane above Everest at sunset, slow pull out

shots.line: What's the longest flight you've ever taken? Tell me in the comments.
shots.scene: End screen: 'What's the longest flight you've ever taken?' cast lined up

shots.line: And subscribe, because next, we're finding out what really happens when turbulence hits.
shots.scene: Teaser: plane jolts in a dark storm, 'NEXT: TURBULENCE'
